title: All Reflective Field-widened Unbalanced Interferometer for Quantum Sensing and Communication Applications
authors: Ramy Tannous, Dogan Sinar, Tabitha D. Arulpragasam, Thomas Jennewein
abstract: Interference of time-bin encoded signals over free-space optical channels typically requires stringent mode filtering on receivers due to wavefront distortions from atmospheric turbulence, conventionally addressed with adaptive optics. Passive multimode receivers based on field-widened interferometers present a compelling alternative, enabling direct interference without the overhead of wavefront correction. We demonstrate a field-widened interferometer design that is implemented solely with reflective surfaces and achieves a high interference visibility (greater than 0.97) for spatially multimode beams. The interference of the multimode beams is enabled by two imaging systems that consist of a cavity configuration between a spherical concave mirror and a flat mirror. The configuration enables small form-factors, is inherently achromatic, and is based on standard spherical mirrors which reduces the complexity of the system. The interferometer is applicable for spatially multimode and turbulent optical channels, such as satellite communication, and is designed for quantum systems that use time-bin encoded qubits.
summary: This paper introduces an all-reflective interferometer designed to overcome wavefront distortion issues inherent in free-space quantum communication. By using only mirrors, the device maintains high interference visibility and remains achromatic across broadband light sources. This makes it a robust alternative to traditional interferometers for applications like satellite quantum links.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is developing passive interferometers for free-space quantum communication that can operate reliably over turbulent atmospheric channels without complex adaptive optics.
main_result: The proposed all-reflective interferometer achieves high interference visibility (>0.97) for spatially multimode beams and is inherently achromatic across broadband wavelengths, outperforming refractive alternatives.
method: The authors employed numerical optical ray tracing simulations to model the performance of their novel reflective interferometer design (Offner Relay Interferometer).
model_or_system: The core system is an All Reflective Field-widened Unbalanced Interferometer utilizing only standard spherical mirrors in a cavity configuration. This setup is designed for time-bin encoded qubits used in quantum communication.
key_observables: Interference visibility (V), physical footprint, and chromatic dependence of the interference signal across broadband wavelengths (600 nm to 1000 nm).
important_parameters: High visibility (>0.97); achromatic performance; ability to handle spatially multimode beams.
main_assumptions: The design is assumed to be limited by beam clipping in the horizontal direction and that refractive interferometers suffer from significant chromatic dispersion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ORI schematic, simulated interference maxima/minima showing high visibility even with angular offsets, and comparisons demonstrating the ORI's wavelength independence versus dispersive glass setups. Other figures show imaging capabilities.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need for turbulence-resistant quantum links, presents the reflective Offner Relay Interferometer (ORI) design, validates its performance via simulations against refractive and standard Michelson designs, and demonstrates its applicability in sensing and communication contexts.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in quantum networking by proposing a robust, passive optical element suitable for field-free propagation channels, which is crucial for scaling up quantum information infrastructure.
